lit-crit-01-c3.text: Scott Bartling (2015). Beyond Language: Viktor Shklovsky, Estrangement, and the Search for Meaning in Art. PhD dissertation, Department of Slavic Languages and Literatures, Stanford University.
lit-crit-01-c3.quote: Russian Formalism was a school of criticism that formed around 1915-1916 and lasted until around 1930, after state suppression and the emigration of some of its leading members effectively put an end to its further development in the Soviet Union.
lit-crit-01-c3.claim: Earlier, and in parallel, came Russian Formalism, active roughly 1915-1930.

lit-crit-01-c3.text: Scott Bartling (2015). Beyond Language: Viktor Shklovsky, Estrangement, and the Search for Meaning in Art. PhD dissertation, Department of Slavic Languages and Literatures, Stanford University.
lit-crit-01-c3.quote: Its insights fared better in the West: Jakobson, who emigrated to Prague in 1920, was able to develop his version of Formalism with the members of the Prague Linguistic Circle under conditions of greater autonomy.
lit-crit-01-c3.claim: Many of its insights survived through Jakobson's later work in Prague and the United States, and they fed into structuralism.

lit-crit-02-c3.text: Lawlor, Leonard (2006). Jacques Derrida. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
lit-crit-02-c3.quote: In 1967 (at the age of thirty-seven), Derrida has his “annus mirabilis,” publishing three books at once: Writing and Difference, Voice and Phenomenon, and Of Grammatology.
lit-crit-02-c3.claim: Jacques Derrida's 1967 trio (Of Grammatology, Writing and Difference, Speech and Phenomena) launched deconstruction.

lit-crit-03-c3.text: Celikates, Robin, Flynn, Jeffrey (2023). Critical Theory. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
lit-crit-03-c3.quote: By contrast to orthodox Marxist dismissal of cultural analysis for focusing on the less consequential “superstructure” of society, Frankfurt School theorists attentively analyzed the form and content of cultural objects
lit-crit-03-c3.claim: The Frankfurt School took Marxist aesthetics in a different direction.

lit-crit-03-c3.text: Celikates, Robin, Flynn, Jeffrey (2023). Critical Theory. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
lit-crit-03-c3.quote: Benjamin posited, in his famous essay, “The Work of Art in the Age of Technological Reproducibility” (1936), that the rise of technologies for mechanical reproduction, such as photography and film, led to the decline of the “aura”
lit-crit-03-c3.claim: Walter Benjamin's 'The Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction' (1936) analysed how new media (photography, film) changed art's social function.

lit-crit-05-c1.text: Bergoffen, Debra, Burke, Megan (2004). Simone de Beauvoir. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
lit-crit-05-c1.quote: She is best known for her trailblazing work in feminist philosophy, The Second Sex (1949)
lit-crit-05-c1.claim: Simone de Beauvoir's The Second Sex (1949) gave it philosophical foundations.
